full_judgment: 9. The learned Deputy Attorney General submits that as the trial Court on consideration of the evidence arrived at the finding that the Plaintiffs claim of the land on the basis of pattan is not true and that the plaintiffs failed to prove the Dakhilas in accordance with the law and that the Dakhilas were created for the purpose of the suit and that the sub-Divisional Manager of the government acquired Estate has no jurisdiction to correct the revenue record under section 143 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act but the Court of appeal below without adverting to the said findings of the trial Court set 'aside the judgment and decree of the trial Court and the judgment of the appellate Court being not a proper judgment of reversal High Court Division was in error in not interfering with the judgment of the Court of appeal below. that the trial Court having had held that the original and the admitted owners of the property in suit having left the country, the property vested in the Government and the High Court Division as failed to take into consideration the provision of Article 143(I)(e) of the Constitution and as such the High Court Division erred in not setting aside the judgment of the appellate Court and consequent thereupon in not setting aside the findings of the appellate Court that the Government did not produce evidence to establish that the property in suit is a vested property. that the finding of the trial Court as regard possession being based on evidence and that the reasoning given by the trial Court in rejecting the claim of the plaintiffs as regard their possession of the land in suit being backed by cogent, the High Court Division was in error in not setting aside the finding of the Court of appeal below with regard to question of possession of the land in suit.
